kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the section's one seven-row class table.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the table; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The BODY-LANE LADDER reading of the table's own ORGAN SYSTEMS column — FIVE lanes: EYE (atropine, homatropine, tropicamide → 'Produce mydriasis and cycloplegia'), CNS (benztropine/trihexyphenidyl for 'Parkinson disease (“park my Benz”)' + 'Acute dystonia'; scopolamine for 'Motion sickness'), GI (glycopyrrolate's route-split secretions row; hyoscyamine/dicyclomine the IBS antispasmodics), RESPIRATORY (ipratropium/tiotropium → 'COPD, asthma'), GENITOURINARY (the SOFT four → overactive bladder). Every lane name, drug set, and application is the book's own print; the five-lane body-tour compression (eye → brain → gut → airway → bladder) is KYP's.
kypExtensions.rationale: The book prints seven parallel rows over five organ systems; the ladder that sorts any 'which antimuscarinic for which organ' stem by body lane is KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[1] + mnemonics[2] + the visual's five lane cards

kypExtensions.summary: The LOCK-AND-LANE reading — ONE RECEPTOR LOCK (the muscarinic receptor, competitive blockade without activation; the class-name banner 'Muscarinic antagonists' is the page's own header) aimed SEVEN ways: the therapeutic difference between the rows is the LANE, not the mechanism. The printed lane-aimers: glycopyrrolate's route pair ('Parenteral: preoperative use to reduce airway secretions' / 'Oral: reduces drooling, peptic ulcer'), the inhaled respiratory pair (ipratropium/tiotropium, 'Respiratory'), the two CNS entries (benztropine/trihexyphenidyl, scopolamine). The CHEMISTRY behind the aiming (quaternary amines that cannot cross the BBB — glycopyrrolate, ipratropium, tiotropium; the tertiary amine that can — scopolamine; the inhaled route's topical delivery) is NOT printed on this page — flagged as KYP wherever used, never cited as printed.
kypExtensions.rationale: The page prints the rows and the route pair but not the structure-property logic behind lane selectivity; the lock-and-lane frame and the chemistry flags are KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[0] + mechanisms[1] + traps + the visual's lock strip

kypExtensions.summary: The DRY-MIRROR frame — what the class does when blockade LEAKS beyond its lane: the ANTI-DUMBBELSS direction (the printed wet list of book 239, one page back, reversed: miosis → mydriasis, bronchospasm → bronchodilation, bradycardia → tachycardia, secretions pouring → dry mouth/skin, gut cramping → constipation, bladder letting go → retention). BOUNDARY RULE: the PRINTED adverse-effects cell ('↑ body temperature (due to ↓ sweating); ↑ HR; dry mouth; dry, flushed skin; cycloplegia; constipation; disorientation' + the angle-closure/prostatic-hyperplasia/infant-hyperthermia line) and the seven-line anticholinergic mnemonic ('Hot as a hare / Fast as a fiddle / Dry as a bone / Red as a beet / Blind as a bat / Mad as a hatter / Full as a flask') + 'Jimson weed (Datura) → gardener’s pupil (mydriasis)' print in the ATROPINE BLOCK BELOW on this same page — the separate pending 'atropine' topic (PH21) — flagged as the adjacent same-page block wherever this topic needs a printed dry-toxidrome anchor, never cited as this topic's own print (this class table prints USES only, no toxicity column).
kypExtensions.rationale: The wet list is printed one page back (PH19) and the dry list prints one section below (PH21); the mirror frame connecting them across this page's position is KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[1] + traps + mnemonics[3] + the visual's dry-mirror band
